title: Ola Electric Shares Jump 10% on Axis Energy Battery Storage Partnership
excerpt: The EV maker signed an MoU for up to 20 GWh of battery energy storage by 2032, accelerating its pivot from scooters into India's booming energy sector.
body:
• Ola Electric shares surged over 10% after the company signed a memorandum of understanding with Axis Energy for up to 20 GWh of battery energy storage capacity by 2032
  • The partnership marks Ola Electric's push beyond electric scooters into the broader energy storage market, leveraging its in-house battery cell technology
  • Ola Electric operates India's only functioning gigafactory with 6 GWh capacity, with plans to expand to 20 GWh by FY28
  • The company's Ola Shakti residential battery storage system is already in the market, with annual demand expected to reach 5 GWh

Shares of Ola Electric Mobility surged more than 10% on Tuesday after the Bhavish Aggarwal-led company announced a memorandum of understanding with Axis Energy to deploy up to 20 GWh of battery energy storage systems by 2032, signaling the electric vehicle maker's ambitious pivot into India's fast-growing energy storage sector.

The MoU positions Ola Electric as a key player in India's push toward renewable energy integration, where large-scale battery storage is critical to managing intermittent solar and wind generation. Axis Energy will leverage Ola's indigenously developed battery cells for its storage projects.

From Scooters to Storage

The partnership builds on Ola Electric's vertical integration strategy, which began with its Krishnagiri gigafactory in Tamil Nadu—India's only operational lithium-ion cell manufacturing plant. The facility currently has 6 GWh of installed capacity, with expansion plans targeting 12 GWh by July 2027 and 20 GWh by the end of FY28.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Zjo8_AFQ0b4

Through its subsidiary Ola Cell Technologies, the company has commercially deployed its 4680-format Bharat Cell, becoming only the second company after Tesla to do so at scale. A newer 46100 LFP cell, announced earlier this year, promises further cost reductions for both vehicles and storage applications.

"Our priority is to make our own cells go into our automotive business first, and then as the Gigafactory ramp becomes beyond our automotive requirement, we start scaling up Shakti."

— Bhavish Aggarwal, CEO and Founder, Ola Electric

Financial and Strategic Context

Ola Electric has invested approximately ₹5,300 crore across manufacturing, battery technology, and R&D, with the bulk of the investment cycle now complete. The company is also raising ₹2,000 crore for Ola Cell Technologies through a stake sale managed by Avendus and Motilal Oswal, a move that would establish a formal market valuation for its battery manufacturing arm.

Around one-third of the planned 20 GWh capacity—roughly 6.5 GWh—is being earmarked for third-party sales, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. Several global and domestic automakers are currently evaluating Ola's manufacturing operations for potential long-term supply agreements.

The Residential Play

The company's Ola Shakti residential battery energy storage system, launched in October 2025, is already generating demand. Available in capacities ranging from 1.5 kWh (₹29,999) to 9.1 kWh (₹1,59,999), the product targets India's growing rooftop solar market and power backup needs. Ola expects annual demand from Shakti alone to reach 5 GWh within a few years.

What's Next

The energy storage partnership adds a significant new revenue stream for a company that has seen its two-wheeler market share decline from 35.5% to around 15% over the past year. Vehicle registrations fell over 51% year-on-year to 1.99 lakh units in 2025, though monthly registrations have shown a recovery trend, surging 150% month-on-month in March. The stock remains well below its 52-week high of ₹71.25, but investors appear to be pricing in the potential of Ola's diversified energy play.
